bull_bear.body: The company's strong credit rating and stable outlook indicate a low risk profile
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Promoter shareholding of 40.46% (as of 30 June 2026) is set to rise to 41.44% upon conversion of warrants issued to promoters.
- ₹500 crores of equity has been infused into the RKFL wheel-manufacturing JV to date, part-funding a ~₹2,000 crore project alongside debt; TRSL-BHEL JV will be funded via 50:50 equity from each partner.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- integration: in-house steel castings for wagon manufacturing — evidence: completed a foundry capacity upgrade to 50,000 metric tonnes per annum, which the company says enables near-complete backward integration for the steel castings it uses in wagons — against it: the MD&A reports an industry-wide forged-wheel shortage in FY26 and says forged wheels and some technology sub-systems are still sourced internationally
- integration: domestic forged-wheel supply through the Ramkrishna Titagarh Rail Wheels joint venture — evidence: the JV is building a large-scale domestic forged-wheel facility, with initial supply commitments to Indian Railways scheduled from FY27 [planned]
- technology: its own TCMS and propulsion capability — evidence: rolled out its first indigenously manufactured driverless metro trainset (Ahmedabad Metro Phase-II) fitted with TCMS for unattended operation; opened a TCMS Laboratory in Bengaluru; dispatched 891 traction motors in FY26 — against it: the advanced TCMS comes through a Transfer of Technology agreement with ABB India, and select technology sub-systems are still imported
- customer lock-in: long-term maintenance tied to its supplies — evidence: the Vande Bharat sleeper project with BHEL covers 80 trains plus maintenance of the trains for 35 years, and the Mumbai Metro Line 5 and Line 6 awards include maintenance — against it: the Vande Bharat project is run as a joint venture with BHEL
- scale: large wagon capacity — evidence: capacity of 12,000 wagons per annum (1,000 per month) — against it: FY26 wagon dispatches were 7,019 units, and the MD&A says standardised wagon types are bought through competitive tenders where technical differentiation is limited
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration in public-sector buyers — A significant share of revenue comes from Indian Railways, metro rail corporations, DFCCIL and other government-linked entities, so a slowdown in public capex, sanctioning delays or a change in procurement policy would hit order inflow hard. The company plans to mitigate this through wagon leasing, exports and more private and international customers.
- Policy and budgetary dependence — Demand depends on the size and pace of the Ministry of Railways' capital programme and on state and city metro budgets, and spending could shift away from conventional rolling stock toward heads such as high-speed rail.
- Forged-wheel and imported-input supply — An industry-wide forged-wheel shortage and changes to wheel specifications constrained FY26 production and can leave existing inventory non-compliant. Forged wheels and some technology sub-systems are still imported, which exposes supply to geopolitical and logistics disruption until domestic capacity (the Ramkrishna Titagarh Rail Wheels JV) is established.
- Execution and scale-up of Passenger Rail Systems — The strategic shift toward passenger rail means scaling coach and metro production sharply from a small base: 63 coach dispatches in FY26 against 12 the year before.
- Working capital and receivables — Long payment cycles from public-sector customers can stretch the working-capital cycle, especially during the passenger-rail ramp-up, which would strain liquidity and increase reliance on external financing.
- Tender-driven pricing and input-cost exposure — Procurement is mainly by competitive tender, which pushes prices down, particularly for standardised wagons where technical differentiation is limited. On fixed-price orders without adequate price-variation clauses, rising steel and specialty-input costs can squeeze margins.
- Technical specification and certification changes — Changing Kavach versions, axle-load norms and safety or emission standards require continuous spending on design, testing and certification, and delays in approvals could hold up order execution.
- Foreign operations and currency — Exposure comes from operating activities and borrowings and is mainly hedged with forward contracts. The company exited its Italian associate Titagarh Firema S.p.A. in FY26 after fully provisioning its exposure, which it expects to reduce this risk.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Diversified rail-systems manufacturer across Freight Rail Systems (FRS), Passenger Rail Systems (PRS) and Shipbuilding & Maritime Systems (via wholly-owned subsidiary Titagarh Naval Systems), with additional JV exposure to forged wheels and Vande Bharat maintenance.
- Company is progressing per its strategic plan and augmenting PRS production capacity, and is preparing to enter the high-speed train segment in a few years.

business.body: Titagarh Rail Systems designs and manufactures freight wagons, bogies and steel castings (Freight Rail Systems) and metro coaches, Vande Bharat and other coach-sets, traction motors, propulsion systems and Train Control and Management Systems (Passenger Rail Systems). Its customers are mainly Indian Railways, metro rail corporations, DFCCIL and private wagon customers. The Shipbuilding & Maritime Systems business was transferred to the wholly-owned subsidiary Titagarh Naval Systems Limited from 1 January 2026, and the company is adding wagon leasing and maintenance services.

- **Passenger Rail Systems:** Metro coaches (incl. aluminium coaches and driverless metro trainsets), Vande Bharat sleeper trains (JV with BHEL), EMUs / MEMUs, Propulsion systems and traction motors, Train Control and Management Systems (TCMS)

outlook.body: Stable outlook; Focus on infrastructure development and transportation
outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body:
- Shift the revenue mix toward Passenger Rail Systems (metro coaches, Vande Bharat, propulsion, TCMS), which the company calls its principal growth engine.
- Backward integration: foundry upgraded to 50,000 metric tonnes per annum for near-complete steel-casting self-sufficiency; domestic forged wheels through the Ramkrishna Titagarh Rail Wheels JV; an aluminium metro-coach manufacturing line under development.
- Technology localisation: Transfer of Technology from ABB India for TCMS, phased localisation of traction converters and motors, and a TCMS Laboratory at the Bengaluru engineering centre.
- Diversify beyond one-off wagon sales into wagon leasing (registered Wagon Leasing Company, first leasing order received) and maintenance services, including a proposed maintenance JV for Vande Bharat trains.
- Focus the listed company on core rail systems by hiving off the Shipbuilding & Maritime Systems business to wholly-owned subsidiary Titagarh Naval Systems Limited from 1 January 2026.
- Reduce customer concentration through exports and, over time, a larger share of private-sector and international customers.
- Exited the Italian associate Titagarh Firema S.p.A. in FY26 to reduce overseas-operations and currency risk.
- Exploratory new-mobility bet: a strategic collaboration with TuTr Hyperloop (IIT Madras incubated) to develop Hyperloop-enabled freight mobility.
- Stayed net-debt negative through the year as part of a stated focus on financial health.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: In FY26 the company finished upgrading its foundry to 50,000 metric tonnes per annum, which it says gives near-complete backward integration for the steel castings used in wagons. It also opened a Vande Bharat production line at its Uttarpara (Kolkata, West Bengal) facility for the 80-train sleeper project run with BHEL. To support the planned Passenger Rail Systems ramp-up, it is developing an integrated facility at Uttarpara with a 1.6 km test track and an aluminium metro-coach manufacturing line that is still under development, backed by a TCMS technology collaboration with ABB. It opened a TCMS Laboratory at its Titagarh Engineering and Technology Centre in Bengaluru to develop TCMS and propulsion systems for the Surat Metro, Ahmedabad Metro, Vande Bharat and ICF EMU/MEMU projects. Under the ABB India agreement it will localise traction converters and motors in phases. Its Ramkrishna Titagarh Rail Wheels joint venture is meant to progressively reduce dependence on imported forged wheels. As a registered Wagon Leasing Company it can now own and lease railway wagons.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Sustained Government investment in railway infrastructure, including rolling stock, signalling, dedicated freight corridors and station modernisation, is expected to support demand for the company's products.
- Expansion of Vande Bharat, Amrit Bharat, metro rail and regional rapid transit projects is expected to drive demand for passenger coaches, propulsion systems and TCMS.
- Growing rail freight capacity from the Dedicated Freight Corridors, and the Government's aim of raising rail's share of freight, are expected to sustain wagon demand.
- Indigenisation under Make in India / Atmanirbhar Bharat and wider adoption of indigenous signalling and digital train-control solutions open room for more value-added products.
- Passenger Rail Systems profitability improved as scale increased; the company is ramping coach production from a small base (63 coach dispatches in FY26 versus 12 in FY25).
- Industry-wide forged-wheel shortages and changes to wheel specifications constrained production schedules in FY26.
- Tender-driven, price-competitive procurement can squeeze margins when raw-material costs rise.
- Exports to South Asia, Africa and South-East Asia are described as a longer-term avenue for diversification.
- Passenger Rail Systems made up approximately 77% of the standalone order book as on 31 March 2026.
- Approximately 6,500 wagons were pending delivery to Indian Railways and private customers as of 31 March 2026, scheduled largely for FY27.
- Letter of Acceptance from NCC Limited for 108 metro coaches (18 trainsets) for Mumbai Metro Line 6, including maintenance, contract value approximately ₹1,598.55 crore.
- Letter of Acceptance from MMRDA for rolling stock and railway systems for Mumbai Metro Line 5, including maintenance, contract value approximately ₹2,481 crore.
- Extension order worth ₹430 crore from Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation for 12 additional Pune Metro trainsets.
- Vande Bharat sleeper project (JV with BHEL): 80 semi high-speed sleeper trains plus 35 years of maintenance.
- First order for Rail Borne Maintenance Vehicles for Indian Railways, and the first wagon-leasing order.
- Diving Support Craft series of five vessels for the Indian Navy: DSC A20 delivered and the third vessel launched.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Titagarh Rail Systems Limited is a leading manufacturer of railway equipment and rolling stock, with a strong credit rating and a stable outlook. The company's products are used in various railway applications, including passenger and freight transportation. With a reaffirmed credit rating of CRISIL AA-/Stable/CRISIL A1+, the company is well-positioned for future growth.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Titagarh Rail Systems designs and manufactures freight wagons, bogies and steel castings (Freight Rail Systems) and metro coaches, Vande Bharat and other coach-sets, traction motors, propulsion systems and Train Control and Management Systems (Passenger Rail Systems). Its customers are mainly Indian Railways, metro rail corporations, DFCCIL and private wagon customers. The Shipbuilding & Maritime Systems business was transferred to the wholly-owned subsidiary Titagarh Naval Systems Limited from 1 January 2026, and the company is adding wagon leasing and maintenance services.

guidance.title: Guidance / outlook
guidance.body: Stable outlook; Focus on infrastructure development and transportation

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Sustained Government investment in railway infrastructure, including rolling stock, signalling, dedicated freight corridors and station modernisation, is expected to support demand for the company's products.
- Expansion of Vande Bharat, Amrit Bharat, metro rail and regional rapid transit projects is expected to drive demand for passenger coaches, propulsion systems and TCMS.
- Growing rail freight capacity from the Dedicated Freight Corridors, and the Government's aim of raising rail's share of freight, are expected to sustain wagon demand.
- Indigenisation under Make in India / Atmanirbhar Bharat and wider adoption of indigenous signalling and digital train-control solutions open room for more value-added products.
- Passenger Rail Systems profitability improved as scale increased; the company is ramping coach production from a small base (63 coach dispatches in FY26 versus 12 in FY25).
- Industry-wide forged-wheel shortages and changes to wheel specifications constrained production schedules in FY26.
- Tender-driven, price-competitive procurement can squeeze margins when raw-material costs rise.
- Exports to South Asia, Africa and South-East Asia are described as a longer-term avenue for diversification.
- Passenger Rail Systems made up approximately 77% of the standalone order book as on 31 March 2026.
- Approximately 6,500 wagons were pending delivery to Indian Railways and private customers as of 31 March 2026, scheduled largely for FY27.
- Letter of Acceptance from NCC Limited for 108 metro coaches (18 trainsets) for Mumbai Metro Line 6, including maintenance, contract value approximately ₹1,598.55 crore.
- Letter of Acceptance from MMRDA for rolling stock and railway systems for Mumbai Metro Line 5, including maintenance, contract value approximately ₹2,481 crore.
- Extension order worth ₹430 crore from Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation for 12 additional Pune Metro trainsets.
- Vande Bharat sleeper project (JV with BHEL): 80 semi high-speed sleeper trains plus 35 years of maintenance.
- First order for Rail Borne Maintenance Vehicles for Indian Railways, and the first wagon-leasing order.
- Diving Support Craft series of five vessels for the Indian Navy: DSC A20 delivered and the third vessel launched.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: In FY26 the company finished upgrading its foundry to 50,000 metric tonnes per annum, which it says gives near-complete backward integration for the steel castings used in wagons. It also opened a Vande Bharat production line at its Uttarpara (Kolkata, West Bengal) facility for the 80-train sleeper project run with BHEL. To support the planned Passenger Rail Systems ramp-up, it is developing an integrated facility at Uttarpara with a 1.6 km test track and an aluminium metro-coach manufacturing line that is still under development, backed by a TCMS technology collaboration with ABB. It opened a TCMS Laboratory at its Titagarh Engineering and Technology Centre in Bengaluru to develop TCMS and propulsion systems for the Surat Metro, Ahmedabad Metro, Vande Bharat and ICF EMU/MEMU projects. Under the ABB India agreement it will localise traction converters and motors in phases. Its Ramkrishna Titagarh Rail Wheels joint venture is meant to progressively reduce dependence on imported forged wheels. As a registered Wagon Leasing Company it can now own and lease railway wagons.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- integration: in-house steel castings for wagon manufacturing — evidence: completed a foundry capacity upgrade to 50,000 metric tonnes per annum, which the company says enables near-complete backward integration for the steel castings it uses in wagons — against it: the MD&A reports an industry-wide forged-wheel shortage in FY26 and says forged wheels and some technology sub-systems are still sourced internationally
- integration: domestic forged-wheel supply through the Ramkrishna Titagarh Rail Wheels joint venture — evidence: the JV is building a large-scale domestic forged-wheel facility, with initial supply commitments to Indian Railways scheduled from FY27 [planned]
- technology: its own TCMS and propulsion capability — evidence: rolled out its first indigenously manufactured driverless metro trainset (Ahmedabad Metro Phase-II) fitted with TCMS for unattended operation; opened a TCMS Laboratory in Bengaluru; dispatched 891 traction motors in FY26 — against it: the advanced TCMS comes through a Transfer of Technology agreement with ABB India, and select technology sub-systems are still imported
- customer lock-in: long-term maintenance tied to its supplies — evidence: the Vande Bharat sleeper project with BHEL covers 80 trains plus maintenance of the trains for 35 years, and the Mumbai Metro Line 5 and Line 6 awards include maintenance — against it: the Vande Bharat project is run as a joint venture with BHEL
- scale: large wagon capacity — evidence: capacity of 12,000 wagons per annum (1,000 per month) — against it: FY26 wagon dispatches were 7,019 units, and the MD&A says standardised wagon types are bought through competitive tenders where technical differentiation is limited

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The company's strong credit rating and stable outlook indicate a low risk profile

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Shift the revenue mix toward Passenger Rail Systems (metro coaches, Vande Bharat, propulsion, TCMS), which the company calls its principal growth engine.
- Backward integration: foundry upgraded to 50,000 metric tonnes per annum for near-complete steel-casting self-sufficiency; domestic forged wheels through the Ramkrishna Titagarh Rail Wheels JV; an aluminium metro-coach manufacturing line under development.
- Technology localisation: Transfer of Technology from ABB India for TCMS, phased localisation of traction converters and motors, and a TCMS Laboratory at the Bengaluru engineering …
